guidance.headline: The best solo opportunity is a narrow, localized utility with a free entry point and a paid trigger tied to an urgent recurring workflow—not a broad app competing on content or features.
guidance.summary: Newcomers are reaching meaningful scale: 380 apps launched in the last 12 months are estimated at $10k+/month, 48 at $100k+/month, and the median newcomer is estimated at $38.4k/month. The strongest investigated movers solve a specific local or workflow gap, such as infrastructure monitoring, meal planning, identity access, or professional measurement, while 363 of 380 products use in-app purchases. Treat all app revenue figures as estimates and validate rank gains with install, conversion, and retention data.

direction.point: Target recurring jobs where mobile users still need a desktop, especially infrastructure, creative, and professional workflows.
direction.evidence: HeC reached #4 in Germany’s Top Grossing Developer Tools after rising 99 places; Supanator rose 128 places to #11 in Indonesia; ProPi rose 127 places to #4 in Indonesia’s Top Paid Utilities; TDInput rose 173 places to #1 in Japan’s Top Paid Developer Tools.

direction.point: Localize around a concrete country-specific need rather than launching a generic global utility.
direction.evidence: Nomor Virtual WhatsApp & WA climbed from #62 to #5 in Indonesia; AOK Ident rose from #67 to #1 in Germany’s Top Free; Gymax rose 174 places to #24 in Indonesia’s Top Grossing Health & Fitness; Eatr rose from #54 to #5 in Indonesia.

direction.point: Build around a daily or weekly action that can become a habit, with widgets, community, rewards, or reminders reinforcing repeat use.
direction.evidence: Widget Al-Qur’an reached #7 in Indonesia’s Top Grossing Lifestyle with 133,427 tracked installs and 8,790 ratings; mise rose 136 places to #6 in Indonesia’s Top Grossing Food & Drink; Kaoポチモ！ went from #134 to #1 in Japan’s Top Free Lifestyle in five days.

growth.point: Launch through the incumbent audience or platform community that already owns the urgent workflow.
growth.evidence: Kaoポチモ！ used check-ins at more than 10,000 drugstores and reached #1 in Japan’s Top Free Lifestyle in five days; AOK Ident’s release coincided with a 66-place rise to #1 in Germany; mystc SA rose 77 places to #11 in Saudi Arabia after a redesign and through its own channels.

growth.point: Use a concrete update—compatibility, reliability, speed, or a redesigned entry point—to create a reason for users to return, then verify whether the gain persists.
growth.evidence: PixieCraft rose 116 places after resolving iOS 27 compatibility issues; AOK Ident reached #1 after identity-confirmation and reliability improvements; Eatr rose 49 places after a faster, less buggy update; Content Manager: AI Сleaner rose 82 places to #8 in Japan after its update.

growth.point: Demonstrate one dramatic outcome with exact setup steps; generic feature promotion is less useful when the acquisition trigger is unknown.
growth.evidence: TDInput positions a setup-light bridge from Apple Watch and iPhone sensors to TouchDesigner and reached #1 in Japan’s Top Paid Developer Tools; Supanator offers mobile Supabase administration but has no identified acquisition source despite a 128-place Indonesian gain.

growth.point: Pair a completed utility action with a reason to return or share.
growth.evidence: mise added community features for sharing dishes and exchanging budget-planning tips, then rose 136 places in Indonesia; Widget Al-Qur’an provides Home Screen and Lock Screen widgets and reached #7 in Indonesia; Kaoポチモ！ turns store visits into redeemable points.

money.point: Use a free entry point and put payment directly after the first useful result; in-app purchases dominate this category.
money.evidence: 363 of 380 products, about 95.5%, use in-app purchases, while 17 use paid upfront; HeC recommends free monitoring with paid forecasting and alerts, while mise is free with in-app purchases and ranks #3 in Germany’s grossing Food & Drink chart.

money.point: For narrow utilities, a one-time purchase can be enough and reduces subscription resistance.
money.evidence: TDInput is priced at ¥150 with no in-app purchases and reached #1 in Japan’s Top Paid Developer Tools; ProPi costs Rp 399 ribu with no in-app purchases and rose 127 places to #4 in Indonesia’s Top Paid Utilities.

money.point: Monetize alerts, forecasting, advanced management, or repeat creation rather than blocking the core task.
money.evidence: HeC places storage-growth, cost, and alerting features in its paid direction; PixieCraft is free with in-app purchases and positions upgrades around repeat creation, export, and craft-building; Gymax is free with in-app purchases but exposes no plan or price, so the conversion wedge still needs testing.

solo.build: Build a localized mobile cost-and-alert companion for a cloud provider used by small teams, with a free health dashboard and one paid storage-cost forecast or proactive alert plan.
solo.avoid: Do not launch another broad AI content, recipe, fitness, or utility app with an unexplained chart spike as validation; these markets already contain products estimated at $740k+/month, including Whipp, mise, TapCook, and VibeShort.
first_week: Interview 10 users of one cloud provider and document the most expensive or most urgent desktop task.
Prototype one free alert: storage growth, projected cost, or downtime.
Add a clearly priced paid forecast or alert feature, then track alert setup, payment conversion, and seven-day return usage.

guidance.headline: Douyin’s fresh-game chart is the clearest near-term opportunity, but treat one-day rank jumps as leads to test—not proof of durable demand or revenue.
guidance.summary: The category has 140 chart slots, 111 distinct games, and 78 publishers, with casual games forming the largest named genre at 48. Three products made large one-day fresh-game jumps—无尽火线 +64 places, 暴走植物园 +77, and 过关天才 +45—but the evidence does not identify their growth mechanisms or retention. For a solo builder, the actionable move is to test a simple, visually clear mechanic during a chart launch window and measure attributable starts before scaling.

direction.point: Start with a simple, low-friction casual mechanic while Douyin’s fresh-game chart can still provide discovery; 过关天才’s 45-place rise to #20 after being described as a non-taxing storage game supports testing clarity and ease of entry rather than building a complex RPG.
direction.evidence: The category has 48 休闲 games versus 26 in the next named genre and 12 合成 games. 过关天才 moved from #65 to #20 on Douyin’s fresh-game chart in one day.

direction.point: Look for a distinct audience or core loop rather than directly entering the established xianxia RPG lane, because a top-five incumbent already occupies that position. A solo builder should compete on differentiation rather than ad budget.
direction.evidence: 灵画师 is described as a leading xianxia RPG with reported 千万+ monthly revenue and remains #4 on the bestseller chart despite slipping 3 places.

direction.point: Build around mechanics that can be understood in a short video: 暴走植物园 and 脑子一团火 both reached #2 on their respective Douyin charts, indicating that simple concepts can produce rapid chart visibility even though their causes are unknown.
direction.evidence: 暴走植物园 rose from #79 to #2 on the fresh-game chart, a 77-place gain; 脑子一团火 rose from #32 to #2 on the popularity chart.

growth.point: Make the first seconds of a Douyin video demonstrate the complete interaction loop and add a unique trackable link, so you can distinguish real acquisition from views or paid traffic. Test one creative hypothesis at a time rather than cloning a product’s theme.
growth.evidence: 阿皮大冒险 recommends a 15–30 second screen recording of search, fight, and extraction; it rose from #77 to #14 on the bestseller chart. 无尽火线 rose from #68 to #4 on the fresh-game chart, while 最强小队 rose from #18 to #4.

growth.point: Express social or cooperative value immediately if your game depends on invitations, but judge the creative by qualified starts rather than views alone. No specific advertising or organic channel caused the observed rank gains, so the hook must be tested independently.
growth.evidence: 最强小队’s visible acquisition hook is gathering partners, and it gained 14 places from #18 to #4 on Douyin’s fresh-game chart.

growth.point: Require multiple days of chart persistence before adapting a breakout product’s mechanics; a single-day jump could reflect advertising, timing, or an existing audience rather than product demand.
growth.evidence: 三国志幻想大陆 gained 61 places from #72 to #11, but its cause was not established; all investigated breakouts have only one tracked day of history.

money.point: Design monetization only after users understand and complete the core loop; place upgrade or unlock offers at failure and progress pressure points, and validate them through completed-round behavior rather than rank movement alone.
money.evidence: 阿皮大冒险 rose 63 places from #77 to #14 on the bestseller chart, but the evidence provides no prices, packages, free-content boundary, or monetization timing. No investigated product supplies verified revenue figures.

money.point: Do not spend on traffic merely because a product rises on the popularity chart; require a sales-side improvement within 72 hours before committing further budget.
money.evidence: 灵画师 gained 40 places on the popularity chart from #60 to #20 while falling 3 places to #4 on the bestseller chart. Its reported 千万+ monthly revenue predates the spike, and no campaign is documented.

solo.build: Build one low-friction Douyin mini-game this month: a simple collection or organization loop that can be understood and completed in a single short clip, with a free core round and one clearly timed paid unlock.
solo.avoid: Do not clone 灵画师’s xianxia RPG positioning or scale ad spend from a popularity-chart jump; the incumbent was #4 on the bestseller chart while its popularity rank rose to #20 without matching sales movement.
first_week: Write one mechanic sentence and a 15-second opening clip showing the complete loop, following the demonstrated clarity used for 阿皮大冒险.
Publish one measured Douyin release with a unique link and compare qualified starts, completed rounds, and chart movement over at least three days.
Add one low-friction paid unlock at a clear progression or failure point, then keep spending disabled until both starter retention and a sales-side signal are visible.

guidance.headline: Builders should target a narrow, repeatable workflow—especially AI-assisted video or photo transformation—rather than launching another broad all-in-one SaaS.
guidance.summary: Web & SaaS still has meaningful room for focused solo products: 319 indie products have payment-verified MRR, but the median is only $430, while 169 were founded in the last 12 months. The strongest examples pair a legible transformation with an immediate result—ScaleReach.ai repurposes long videos, Boothie transforms selfies, and TrendStory creates short-form clips—while distribution evidence remains weak and should be tested directly rather than assumed.

direction.point: Build around the gap between an existing asset and a specific desired output, not around a generic AI category; the clearest openings are long-to-short video repurposing and one-camera-look photo transformation.
direction.evidence: ScaleReach.ai grew verified MRR from $2,359.26 to $6,176.52 in 8 days; Boothie grew from $37,644.81 to $52,185.27 in 28 days; TrendStory grew from $38,149.23 to $67,035.28 over 30 days. The category also has 23 AI video & UGC ads products, including White Glove Content at $72.4k MRR and TrendStory at $67k.

direction.point: Choose one narrow operational workflow that replaces several manual steps, then make the first useful result the activation moment.
direction.evidence: SmartlyCV bundles resume tailoring, cover letters, interview practice, and application management and grew verified MRR from $61.70 to $450.44 over 30 days; Superjoin combines HubSpot, Salesforce, and 30+ integrations with Sheets and Excel and reached $96,757 verified MRR. Neither result proves the bundle caused the growth.

direction.point: Avoid undifferentiated AI assistants and broad productivity apps unless you can name a frequent job and own a reachable audience.
direction.evidence: AI assistants & agents has 34 products and phone utilities 14, while the category median verified MRR is only $430. ChadMe reached $648.16 verified MRR, but its acquisition source was not found.

growth.point: Turn the output into a before-and-after demonstration and publish it where the exact problem is already discussed; community demand is useful as a test pool, not proof of acquisition.
growth.evidence: Boothie reached $52,185.27 MRR while photography discussion rose from 2 to 13 threads in 14-day windows; ScaleReach.ai reached $6,176.52 MRR while NewTubers had 19 relevant threads versus 0 previously. No evidence links either product directly to those discussions.

growth.point: Use free search discovery to capture high-intent utility tasks, but begin with one narrowly ranked utility rather than a broad toolbox.
growth.evidence: IT Tools improved web traffic rank from 270,251 to 57,936 in 7 days and self-hosted discussion rose from 2 to 20 threads; Thakor Editz entered the top 1M at rank 280,449 within two tracked days.

growth.point: Make the result inherently shareable when the product is a simulator, quiz, or generator; the hook should invite another person to take the same action.
growth.evidence: 1 in 8 Billion improved web traffic rank from 134,634 to 28,922 in seven days, while relevant discussion rose from 1 to 7 threads; YouTest.me uses the explicit prompt of choosing a friendship test.

money.point: Let users experience the core result before charging, then put recurring subscription checkout immediately after the first useful output.
money.evidence: Draftly grew from $14,404.07 to $21,910.27 verified MRR over 30 days after offering a one-prompt website workflow; TrendStory reached $67,035.28 MRR after a one-to-few-clicks short-video workflow. Neither evidence set confirms the exact paywall timing or price.

money.point: Bundle adjacent steps into one recurring subscription instead of selling isolated outputs, especially when the tool supports repeated use.
money.evidence: SmartlyCV reached $450.44 verified MRR from $61.70 by packaging resume tailoring, cover letters, interview practice, and application management; NeoScene grew from $329.90 to $3,654 verified MRR by placing subscriptions inside photo-to-video conversion.

money.point: Price a clearly installed utility as a monthly service, but only if the setup or recurring benefit is specific enough to explain that cadence.
money.evidence: INXANITY Labs pairs a free browser-game directory with a $19.99/month Windows launcher for one-click AI-built game mods; helumi grew verified MRR from $93.48 to $533.48 in 18 days with an instant-access cloud drive finder for Mac.

solo.build: Build a one-input web app that turns a long video into three platform-ready short clips, starting with YouTube-to-TikTok/Reels/Shorts export, a visible review step, and one subscription plan.
solo.avoid: Do not ship a generic AI-video studio or clone a broad list of integrations; the growth trigger is still unresolved for ScaleReach.ai, TrendStory, Superjoin, and other products, so a narrow workflow must prove repeat use and paid conversion first.
first_week: Interview five creators or marketers and collect one real long video each, then define the exact clips they would publish.
Build the smallest version that detects strong moments, lets the user edit them, and exports one vertical clip.
Launch to 20 qualified creators or marketers with a free first export, then track activation, second export, and paid conversion.

guidance.headline: Chrome’s clearest opportunity for a solo builder is a narrow, high-frequency browser intervention—translation, screening, or workflow enhancement—because only 52 featured extensions were published in the last two years despite 132 reaching 1M+ users.
guidance.summary: Demand is concentrated in extensions that save time or reduce friction inside existing browser workflows: translation, shopping cleanup, security audits, and travel search each reached 100,000–6,000,000 verified users. Recent entrants can gain traction with a focused utility rather than a broad browser suite, although the category’s recent median is only 3,000 users, making distribution and a crisp use case essential.

direction.point: Look for underserved, task-specific problems inside already-popular sites rather than building another all-purpose productivity extension; focused entrants have reached substantial scale, including Amazon search filtering at 100,000 users and award-seat search across Google Flights, Chase Travel, and Amex Travel at 100,000 users.
direction.evidence: Knockoff - Amazon Shopping Filter has 100,000 verified users; seats.aero has 100,000; only 52 of 582 featured extensions were published in the last two years.

direction.point: Prioritize workflows where users already feel blocked by language, clutter, or trust: document translation is the strongest recent example, while extension auditing and shopping cleanup address immediate friction.
direction.evidence: AnyDoc Translator has 6,000,000 verified users and preserves document layouts with bilingual subtitles; Extension Auditor has 200,000 users; Knockoff has 100,000.

direction.point: A useful angle can be emotionally distinctive rather than technically deep: Cat Gatekeeper turns a forced break from social media into a cat-themed screen intervention and reached 300,000 users.
direction.evidence: Cat Gatekeeper has 300,000 verified users; the recent-extension median is 3,000 users, so a memorable hook can help a small product stand out.

growth.point: Attach the extension directly to a recognizable service or repeated task so its value is obvious from the search result and first use; this approach is visible in translation, Amazon filtering, and travel-award search.
growth.evidence: AnyDoc Translator reached 6,000,000 verified users; Knockoff - Amazon Shopping Filter and seats.aero each reached 100,000.

growth.point: Use a narrowly defined audience and a specific trigger to create sharing and habitual return behavior; the strongest recent example interrupts social-media use with a playful pet mechanic.
growth.evidence: Cat Gatekeeper reached 300,000 verified users in 211 days; EXT — Faceit Intelligence and Geometry Dash Lite Game each reached 100,000.

growth.point: Optimize for visible, one-sentence outcomes rather than feature breadth, because marketplace success can follow immediately after launch even without a recorded user change.
growth.evidence: Google Vids Screen Recorder reached 300,000 users; MYNT: Material You New Tab reached 200,000; ZeroDelay reached 100,000, and all three show recorded change of 0.

money.point: Treat monetization as an unvalidated open question in this dataset and test willingness to pay only after establishing repeat use; no investigated products, monetization moves, prices, or revenue figures were supplied.
money.evidence: All 12 recent products have null USD values and empty price fields; the category statistics contain user counts but no verified pricing or revenue data.

money.point: Avoid assuming that large audience size automatically supports a paid extension: even a 6,000,000-user product may be free, while the most recent products have only 100,000–300,000 users.
money.evidence: AnyDoc Translator has 6,000,000 verified users but no listed price; Cat Gatekeeper has 300,000 and Google Vids Screen Recorder has 300,000, both with no listed price.

money.point: If charging, test a simple paid tier for an ongoing utility after usage proves habitual, but validate the offer with users because the input provides no observed price shape or paying-customer evidence.
money.evidence: The supplied category contains 582 tracked extensions, 132 with 1M+ users, and 52 published in the last two years, but no product prices, revenue estimates, or monetization moves.

solo.build: Build a browser extension that searches and translates award availability across travel sites, improving on seats.aero with one concrete workflow such as alerts, comparison, or a clearer results view; start with a single recurring traveler use case rather than a full travel suite.
solo.avoid: Do not launch a broad productivity suite with an untested paid subscription: the input provides no pricing evidence, and the median among recent extensions is only 3,000 users.
first_week: Interview five frequent travelers about how they currently check award seats and identify the slowest repeated step.
Build one narrow end-to-end flow over Google Flights, then add Chase Travel or Amex Travel only after the first flow works.
Release the single-site MVP with a clear before/after demo, then test an optional paid alert tier before expanding scope.

guidance.headline: Shopify’s clearest solo-builder opportunity is a narrow, compliance- or revenue-triggered seller tool that earns attention quickly and monetizes through a free-to-paid tier.
guidance.summary: The category is crowded at the top but still shows room in focused operational niches: 4 of the newer $10k+ apps sit in E-commerce & seller tools, while Judge.me Email Marketing opened a new lane in newsletters with an estimated $17k. A free-entry model dominates—87% of 410 tracked apps use free plans with paid tiers—so builders should pair immediate merchant utility with a clear upgrade path rather than charge before value is visible.

direction.point: Look for narrow Shopify compliance and operations jobs where a deadline can drive adoption; Revoq’s EU withdrawal button is the strongest new signal, reaching an estimated $102.5k from 586 reviews.
direction.evidence: Revoq ‑ EU Withdrawal Button: estimated $102.5k, 586 reviews, free plan available; the lane also contains RF: Barcode Labels Generator at an estimated $123.4k.

direction.point: Prioritize tools that directly support store revenue or merchandising rather than broad all-in-one platforms; the established leaders are concentrated in reviews, subscriptions, bundles, sourcing, and landing-page conversion.
direction.evidence: Judge.me Product Reviews App (estimated $8.83M), Appstle Subscriptions (estimated $1.63M), Kaching Bundles & Upsells (estimated $1.19M), and DSers (estimated $1.13M).

direction.point: Test email tooling as a focused standalone wedge, because the newsletter lane has only 9 tracked apps and its new entrant reached an estimated $17k with 97 reviews.
direction.evidence: Judge.me Email Marketing: estimated $17k, 97 reviews, free to install; Newsletters & email marketing has 9 tracked apps, including Pop Convert at an estimated $1.52M.

direction.point: Avoid entering broad AI or social-ad categories until you can name a specific merchant workflow; recent AI and social entries show attention, but the revenue signals in this sample remain weak or absent.
direction.evidence: ChatGPT and RepOcean Google Reviews are both free with no revenue estimate reported; the AI video & UGC ads and Social media management lanes each have only 12 and 5 tracked apps, respectively.

growth.point: Make the app installable for free and useful within minutes, then let merchant activity expose the need for paid features; the category’s dominant pattern is free acquisition followed by upgrades.
growth.evidence: 358 of 410 apps use a free plan plus paid tiers (87%); Judge.me Email Marketing is free to install and has 97 reviews, while Revoq promises setup in minutes and has 586 reviews.

growth.point: Use marketplace reviews and visible merchant outcomes as the acquisition engine, especially for utility tools whose value can be understood from the listing alone.
growth.evidence: Judge.me Product Reviews App has 50,464 reviews and an estimated $8.83M; TikTok has 15,951 reviews and an estimated $2.79M; Loox has 10,148 reviews and an estimated $1.78M.

growth.point: Cross-sell from an existing app ecosystem or bundle email, review, and conversion workflows; several leaders have expanded into adjacent revenue-driving functions rather than relying on one isolated feature.
growth.evidence: Judge.me spans product reviews and email marketing; Pop Convert, estimated $1.52M, combines popups, banners, and email-list building; PageFly covers page building, leak detection, and A/B testing.

growth.point: Build for a visible trigger such as an EU compliance deadline, not a generic merchant pain; immediate relevance should make installation and review requests easier to earn.
growth.evidence: Revoq targets the June 19, 2026 EU requirement, says setup takes minutes, and has 586 reviews plus an estimated $102.5k.

money.point: Start free, then charge merchants when they gain a recurring or scale-dependent benefit; this matches the dominant category model and lowers the barrier to getting reviews.
money.evidence: 358 of 410 apps (87%) use free-plus-paid pricing; Revoq, Trustpilot, Judge.me Product Reviews App, Loox, and Appstle all offer a free plan or free entry.

money.point: Price the upgrade around operational value and merchant scale rather than charging simply for installation; products tied to conversion, subscriptions, or merchant volume offer a clearer path to expansion.
money.evidence: Stamped starts at $23/month and has an estimated $1.73M; Snowball starts at $249/month and has an estimated $1.06M, showing that higher monthly pricing can work when tied to a substantial marketing outcome.

money.point: Use monthly recurring pricing for ongoing merchant workflows, but only after the free tier demonstrates value; the observed examples do not favor one-time purchase pricing for the strongest apps.
money.evidence: Stamped is from $23/month and Snowball is from $249/month, while the dominant free-plus-paid cohort includes Judge.me Product Reviews App, Loox, Pop Convert, DSers, and PageFly.

solo.build: Build a focused EU compliance checklist app for Shopify merchants that detects missing withdrawal, consumer-rights, and shipping disclosures, then offers paid automated monitoring and implementation guidance.
solo.avoid: Do not build another generic email-marketing suite, review widget, or AI ad generator; Judge.me Email Marketing already covers email with 97 reviews, while ChatGPT and RepOcean show no reported revenue estimate.
first_week: Interview 10 EU Shopify merchants about their withdrawal-button and disclosure workflow, including Revoq’s June 19, 2026 requirement.
Ship a thin checklist and store-scan prototype that flags one missing compliance element and links merchants to a fix.
Offer the scanner free, then test a paid monitoring tier aimed at stores that need recurring checks and implementation support.
